newsitem.title: FRANCE: French grain in feed up 11 pct, latest data shows.
newsitem.headline: French grain in feed up 11 pct, latest data shows.

text.p: The amount of French grain going into manufactured animal feed remains up on last season but the rate of increase has slowed somewhat, figures released by France's ONIC cereals office showed on Wednesday.
The figures are for usage between the start of the crop marketing year on July 1, 1996, and the beginning of December, the latest period for which data is available.
ONIC said total grain use in compound feed was fractionally over 3.8 million tonnes in the period, up 11.1 percent from 3.42 million tonnes in the same five months of 1995.
In the four months to November 1 the annual percentage increase had been higher at 13.6 percent.
Barley showed the strongest annual increase of 46.9 percent to reach 465,400 tonnes between July 1 and December 1, but the gain was down from 56.7 percent between July 1 and November 1.
ONIC said the increases reflected "good supplies" to the internal market in the wake of bumper crops last year.

This was helping France and other European Union states to carry out one of the primary aims of the 1992 Common Agricultural Policy reform -- recapturing internal markets for grain which had previously been depressed by high imports of alternative ingredients like corn gluten feed.
For the whole season between July and June, ONIC projects a 12 percent increase in total cereals usage for manufactured feed to some 9.4 million tonnes from 8.37 million in 1995/96.
In 1992/93, the last year before the CAP reform went into effect, the figure was just 5.6 million tonnes.
